statements.subject: server
statements.description: The CHILDREN return option is simply an indication that the client wants information about whether or not mailboxes contain child mailboxes; a server MAY provide it even if the option is not specified.
statements.trigger: LIST command received without CHILDREN return option
actions: include \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren attributes in LIST response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The CHILDREN return option defines two new attributes that MUST be returned within a LIST response: \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Although these attributes MAY be returned in response to any LIST command, the CHILDREN return option is provided to indicate that the client particularly wants this information.
actions: include \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren attributes in LIST response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the CHILDREN return option is present, the server MUST return these attributes even if their computation is expensive.
statements.trigger: LIST command received with CHILDREN return option
actions: return \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren attributes in LIST response regardless of computation cost

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT set this attribute if there are child mailboxes and the user does not have permission to access any of them.
statements.trigger: LIST response generation with \HasChildren attribute evaluation
actions: omit \HasChildren attribute from LIST response when user lacks permission to all child mailboxes

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In this case, \HasNoChildren SHOULD be used.
statements.trigger: LIST response generation when user lacks permission to all child mailboxes
